question: does a C below the old grid minimum (0.01) improve B1's mean LOSO macro-F1?
motivation: results/baseline_loso.json (R2, pipeline view): C 0.01 -> 0.638, 0.1 -> 0.517, 1 -> 0.497, 10 -> 0.469; the score rises monotonically as C shrinks and the grid stopped at 0.01
model: tools.train_baseline.make_pipe(C): StandardScaler + LogisticRegression(C, max_iter=5000, class_weight='balanced') on Lab_hist

edge_rule.if: the best sweep C is the smallest grid value
edge_rule.note: declared here so an extension is not a post-hoc choice; no further extension

data: reference feature cache (results/baseline_loso.json), exact R2 cap video_cap_mask(seed=20261006), 3395 trainval images, 4 outer folds
sweep: fixed C for all folds, temperature 1, scored on the LOSO holdouts; every C is reported

nested.selection: per outer fold on the inner validation: macro-F1, then calibrated NLL, then grid order (ascending C, so the smaller C wins ties)
nested.inner_split: tools.compare_tabular.inner_split with the group guard; seeds 20261006/20261007/20261008 change only the inner split
nested.temperature: chosen on the same inner validation from [0.5, 0.75, 1, 1.5, 2, 3, 5]

metric: tools.summarize_runs.evaluate (fold_table + calibration); primary = mean LOSO macro-F1

decision_rule.primary: nested: mean over 3 seeds of mean LOSO macro-F1 > B1 (0.6381973706626417)
decision_rule.secondary: sweep under the original deploy rule: mean LOSO macro-F1 rounded to 2 decimals, then the smaller C
decision_rule.reading: a sweep-only gain is selection on the holdouts (as the original C choice was) and needs the nested result or new data to back it

limits: LOSO source-level convenience dataset; no Pi/E2E/frozen-test claim; inner groups and manifest are the regenerated copies that reproduce the tracked B1 numbers exactly (results/ensemble_b1_keras_20261011)
